According to the latest report from Bloomberg, Phil Schiller will step down from his role overseeing the App Store and Apple Events. This move marks the latest development in his decades-long tenure at Apple.

Phil Schiller to remain as an "Apple Fellow" for now

Schiller served as Apple's Senior Vice President of Worldwide Marketing until 2020, after which he transitioned to the newly created title of "Apple Fellow." Greg Joswiak took over as Senior Vice President of Marketing at that time.

When Apple announced Schiller's transition to Apple Fellow, the company stated that he would continue to lead the App Store and Apple Events. The Wall Street Journal reported in 2024 that Schiller was still working nearly 80 hours per week at that time.

Despite stepping down from his leadership of the App Store and Apple Events, Schiller will remain an Apple Fellow and participate in "unspecified projects." However, the report notes that employees within Apple view this move as a "big step" toward Schiller's eventual retirement.

Alongside Schiller's departure, Bloomberg reports that Apple is shifting leadership of these areas to its services division under Eddy Cue.

With the latest changes, Apple is placing App Store management under its services division led by executive Eddy Cue. Cue previously oversaw the App Store in its early years, before the role was handed to Schiller and the marketing team in 2015. According to Bloomberg, Cue is taking on a more influential role under Ternus's leadership. On a day-to-day basis, the App Store will be managed by Carson Oliver, a senior member of the division who now reports directly to Cue. Two years ago, Schiller had split App Store responsibilities between two direct reports: Oliver and Ann Thai.

Leadership of Apple Events will be taken over by Nola Weinstein, who "has overseen the area as Schiller's deputy since 2023." Weinstein will report to Kristin Huguet Quayle, Apple's Vice President of Communications and Public Relations.

The biggest news today is, of course, that today is Tim Cook's final day as Apple's CEO. John Ternus officially takes the reins on Tuesday. Cook issued an internal memo to all employees on the day of his farewell from the Apple CEO role to mark the occasion, the contents of which can be read here.
